summary.name: Cyberpunk. Supplemental design reference in the Digital and 3D Aesthetics category, not claimed as a directly named style in the source collection.
summary.visualIdentity: Technology-dense setting with legible social and industrial character, controlled neon, atmosphere and localized reflections. The subject needs a clear luminance hierarchy. Devices, streets or signal systems should visibly function, not rely only on purple-blue light, signs or decorative HUDs.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: world-building scenes with a strong environment, sci-fi story trailers, speculative product narratives, hacking sequences and transitions. Stated HTML use: an interactive scene page with keyboard-focusable DOM HUD panels. Other genres or audiences are unspecified and inferred only.
summary.limitations: Supplemental reference with no directly named source-collection authority. Decorative HUDs, sign-only light, constant corruption, strobing, floating HUD clutter and purple-blue wash are excluded. Two-color contrast checks do not verify text over glass, video or animated light. Simulated appearance is not physical validation.
summary.palette: Background policy is scene_dependent; #111D25 is an illustrative swatch, not a required canvas color. Suggested status is style-compatible, not approved: foreground #F1F0E3, accent_1 #52B3AC, accent_2 #DAA259, accent_3 #B96887. Foreground on background measures 14.934. Accent_1 and accent_2 carry background-colored text (6.852, 7.578). Accent_3 (4.398) is decorative only. Gradients are disabled. Task-provided exact colors override these and must not be altered. Recheck contrast on composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion references are optional and need scene-specific support. motion-012 (chapter handoff) and motion-015 (story orchestration) suit chaptered narratives. motion-020 glitch cut is compatible but only for intentional disruption. motion-037 and motion-039 apply only with real device, sign copy or an approved mark, and must avoid HUD spectacle. Video runs on deterministic composition time; interactive delivery may use scroll or pointer and needs reduced-motion stills.
summary.audio: Audio is unspecified and not mandated; no tempo, instrument or voice is assigned. Inferred options: restrained ambience or device sound accents that clarify functioning hardware and transitions, with music or voice only if the brief asks. Silence and reading holds are valid. Gallery previews stay silent. Do not invent audio or claim beat or speech sync without inspected audio.
summary.assetRequirements: No uploads are specified. Needed inputs are in-world devices, streets or signal systems with defined light sources, fog, PBR materials and any inspected approved mark or copy. Do not invent brand marks or product copy. Load local fonts and assets before rendering. Asset formats, dimensions and exact copy are unspecified.
summary.combinations: Style-112 (diegetic interfaces) is recommended for story trailers: HUD panels attach to in-world sources, neon is limited to defined sources and the subject stays brightest. Style-067 (signal-intrusion punctuation) fits only at cuts or story events, using primary accents and never constant corruption. Cyberpunk alone is preferred for strong-environment world-building.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary composition and export pipeline. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. Three.js with PBR materials and postprocessing should own visual rendering. GSAP should own motion on one paused seekable timeline. SVG or HTML handles readable text. chroma-js is optional for validation. Verify seeks, frames and audio.
